ownership: Mixed-economy public company (B3: BBAS3); Federal Government controlling shareholder (~50%)
controlling: União Federal (Brazilian Federal Government) — controlling shareholder with ~50% of capital
shareholders: Free float (~49.6% — Brazilian and foreign investors)
business_focus: Universal bank: retail, wholesale, agribusiness (largest rural-credit franchise in Brazil), government services, asset management, insurance (BB Seguridade) and payments
history: Founded 12 October 1808 by Dom João VI in Rio de Janeiro — the oldest bank in continuous operation in Brazil and among the oldest in the Americas. Evolved into a mixed-economy listed company with the Federal Government as controlling shareholder. Head office is in Brasília (Setor de Autarquias Norte). Systemically important Brazilian bank with a nationwide branch and digital franchise and a leading role in agribusiness credit.
context: Typically among Brazil’s top banks by assets and equity (with Itaú, Bradesco, Caixa and Santander). Peer set is the large Brazilian universal banks; competitive edge in agribusiness and public-sector relationships.

sources.label: Banco do Brasil Reference Form / IR

legal_name: Itaú Unibanco Holding S.A. / Itaú Unibanco S.A.
ownership: Public (B3 / NYSE: ITUB); joint control via IUPAR / Itaúsa / Companhia E. Johnston
controlling: IUPAR (Itaú Unibanco Participações), Itaúsa and Companhia E. Johnston — Villela/Setubal and Moreira Salles family control structure
shareholders: IUPAR — Itaú Unibanco Participações S.A. (joint control)
Companhia E. Johnston de Participações (joint control)
business_focus: Universal bank: mass and premium retail, SME, corporate & investment banking (Itaú BBA), asset management, insurance distribution and LatAm affiliates
history: Formed by the 2008 Itaú–Unibanco merger (roots: Banco Itaú 1945; Unibanco from Casa Moreira Salles 1924). Largest private Brazilian bank by many franchise metrics. HQ at Praça Alfredo Egydio de Souza Aranha, São Paulo.
context: Primary peer of Banco do Brasil, Bradesco and Santander Brasil in the Brazilian commercial-banking oligopoly; usually leads private banks by market capitalization.

ownership: Public (B3: BBDC3/BBDC4; NYSE: BBD); concentrated control block + free float
controlling: Long-standing Cidade de Deus / Fundação Bradesco-linked control structure (voting control block)
shareholders: Control block associated with Cidade de Deus / Fundação Bradesco structures
business_focus: Universal bank with large insurance/pension franchise (Bradesco Seguros): retail, SME, corporate, cards, asset management
hq_city: Osasco (Cidade de Deus, São Paulo state)
history: Founded 10 March 1943 by Amador Aguiar in Marília (SP) as Banco Brasileiro de Descontos. HQ moved to Cidade de Deus, Osasco. One of Brazil’s largest private banks with a deep insurance cross-sell platform.
context: Competes directly with Itaú and Banco do Brasil for mass retail and insurance distribution; often #3–4 by equity/assets among Brazilian banks.

employees_as_of: ~2021 company / public disclosures (order of magnitude; verify latest IR)
business_focus: Public universal bank: housing/mortgage (FGTS), savings, social programs, lotteries, retail and SME credit; strong government-policy role
history: Founded 12 January 1861 by Emperor Pedro II in Rio de Janeiro as a savings institution. Consolidated into present-day Caixa Econômica Federal; headquartered in Brasília. Largest fully government-owned bank in Latin America and a core channel for Brazilian housing finance and social programs.
context: Peer of BB on the public side of Brazilian banking; largest mortgage/FGTS franchise. Not listed — ownership is entirely federal.

founded: 1982 (Santander franchise in Brazil; major scale via Banespa and other acquisitions)
ownership: Public subsidiary of Banco Santander S.A. (Spain) — B3: SANB11 / NYSE: BSBR
employees_as_of: 2025 management report (group employees in Brazil franchise)
business_focus: Universal commercial bank: retail, consumer finance, SME, wholesale/CIB, cards and payments (Getnet adjacency)
history: Santander entered Brazil in the 1980s and built scale through acquisitions culminating in Banespa (2000) and the ABN AMRO Brazil franchise. Headquartered in São Paulo (Av. Juscelino Kubitschek). Largest Santander Group franchise outside Europe by contribution.
context: Fifth large Brazilian universal bank; Spanish origin distinguishes it from locally controlled peers Itaú/Bradesco/BB/Caixa.

ownership: Public (B3: BPAC11); partnership / controlling partners + free float
controlling: Controlling partnership around founding/senior partners (incl. André Esteves as leading partner historically)
business_focus: Investment bank + wealth/asset management with expanding commercial and digital retail banking
history: Founded 1983 in Rio de Janeiro as an investment bank; today headquartered in São Paulo. Leading Brazilian IB/wealth franchise that expanded into asset management and commercial banking; listed via units on B3.
context: Competes with Itaú BBA, XP and global bulge brackets in IB/wealth; smaller balance sheet than the big-five universal banks but high ROE franchise historically.

ownership: Public (SSE: CHILE); LQ Inversiones Financieras / Quiñenco–Citigroup control structure
controlling: LQ Inversiones Financieras (Quiñenco) with historical Citigroup joint-control arrangements
business_focus: Universal commercial bank: retail, SME, corporate and treasury
history: One of Chile’s oldest commercial banks (1893). Combines a large retail franchise with corporate and treasury businesses. Part of the Quiñenco financial ecosystem with historical Citigroup ties.
context: Top-tier Chilean private bank by equity and loans; core competitor to Santander, BCI and Itaú Chile.

ownership: Public subsidiary of Banco Santander S.A. (Spain)
business_focus: Universal bank: retail, consumer lending, SME, corporate and digital banking
history: Chilean unit of the Santander Group. Broad retail and corporate franchise with strong digital and consumer lending presence.
context: Usually among the largest private banks in Chile by assets and customers.

ownership: Public; controlling interest historically linked to the Yarur family / Empresas Juan Yarur
controlling: Yarur family control structure (Empresas Juan Yarur / related holdings)
business_focus: Universal bank: retail, commercial, corporate; also City National Bank of Florida (US subsidiary of the group)
history: Founded 1937 in Santiago. One of Chile’s major private banks; the BCI group also owns City National Bank of Florida in the United States.
context: Peer of Banco de Chile, Santander and Itaú among Chile’s large private banks.

founded: 1953 as BancoEstado (roots 1855 Caja de Crédito Hipotecario)
business_focus: Public universal bank with national coverage emphasis: retail, mortgages, SME, government-related financial services
history: Created in 1953 by merging several state savings/credit institutions whose oldest root is the 1855 Caja de Crédito Hipotecario. Chile’s only fully public commercial bank; HQ at Av. Libertador Bernardo O’Higgins 1111, Santiago.
context: Often among the largest Chilean banks by customers and geographic coverage; peers are the large private banks on franchise size.

business_focus: Corporate, investment-banking adjacency and wealth / private banking (not mass-market retail)
history: Chilean commercial bank of the BTG Pactual group. Focuses on corporate, capital-markets adjacency and wealth rather than mass retail.
context: Niche franchise versus large Chilean universal banks. Origin country is Brazil.

ownership: Subsidiary of The Bank of Nova Scotia (Canada)
shareholders: Bank of Nova Scotia / Nova Scotia Inversiones
business_focus: Universal commercial bank: retail, consumer, SME and corporate
history: Chilean banking unit of Scotiabank (Canada). Built through acquisitions including parts of the former Banco del Desarrollo / Sud Americano franchises over time.
context: Among Chile’s larger private banks; Canadian origin parent.

founded: Chile franchise via Corpbanca / Itaú merger path
business_focus: Universal commercial bank in Chile under the Itaú brand
history: Itaú’s Chilean bank after the combination with Corpbanca. Brazilian-origin franchise competing in Chile’s large-bank peer set.
context: Brazilian origin; peers are Banco de Chile, Santander, BCI and Scotiabank.

founded: 1875 (as Banco de Colombia; Bancolombia brand after 1998 merger)
ownership: Public (BVC / NYSE ADR CIB); parent holding Grupo Cibest (2025 reorganization)
controlling: Grupo Cibest / historical Grupo Sura–Argos ecosystem influence
shareholders: Institutional and free float (BVC / NYSE: CIB)
business_focus: Universal bank: retail, SME, corporate, leasing, trust, investment and Central American affiliates
history: Roots in Banco de Colombia (1875). 1998 merger of Banco de Colombia and Banco Industrial Colombiano created Bancolombia. Colombia’s largest bank by assets. HQ in Medellín. In 2025 the listed holding evolved to Grupo Cibest.
context: Systemically important Colombian bank; primary peers Bogotá, Davivienda and Occidente.

ownership: Public; controlled by Grupo Aval (Sarmiento Angulo)
controlling: Grupo Aval / Luis Carlos Sarmiento Angulo
business_focus: Universal bank: commercial, consumer and mortgage lending; Aval-group flagship
history: Founded 15 November 1870 — Colombia’s oldest commercial bank. Flagship of Grupo Aval. Listed on the BVC.
context: Core Aval bank; peers Bancolombia, Davivienda and Occidente.

ownership: Controlled by Grupo Empresarial Bolívar / Davivienda Group holding
business_focus: Universal bank: retail, mortgage heritage, SME, corporate; Central American franchises
history: Started in 1972 as a savings-and-loan corporation (Corporación de Ahorro y Vivienda) and later became Banco Davivienda. Owned by Grupo Empresarial Bolívar. Regional presence in Central America and the U.S.
context: One of Colombia’s Big-Four banks with Bancolombia, Bogotá and Occidente.

founded: Commercial banking license under BTG franchise (2010s)
business_focus: Investment-banking led franchise expanded into commercial banking and wealth
history: Colombian banking unit of Brazilian BTG Pactual. Capital-markets and wealth oriented versus large retail incumbents.
context: Niche corporate/capital-markets bank. Origin country is Brazil (not Colombia).

founded: BBVA franchise in Colombia (local predecessors earlier)
business_focus: Universal commercial bank under the BBVA brand
history: Colombian unit of Spanish BBVA. Retail and commercial franchise competing with large local banks.
context: Spanish-origin bank in Colombia’s mid-to-large tier.

business_focus: Universal bank: nationwide retail and corporate; Credicorp flagship
history: Founded 1889. Peru’s largest bank and flagship of Credicorp.
context: Leads Peruvian banking by loans and deposits; peers Interbank, BBVA Perú and Scotiabank Perú.

legal_name: Banco de la República Oriental del Uruguay
business_focus: Public commercial bank: retail, government-related franchise, nationwide coverage
history: Uruguay’s largest bank and the main public commercial bank (founded 1896).
context: Systemically important; peers include Itaú Uruguay, Santander and Scotiabank.

business_focus: Commercial and retail banking under the HSBC brand
history: Uruguayan banking subsidiary of HSBC. UK-origin international bank.
context: Foreign-owned mid-size franchise versus BROU and regional peers.

business_focus: Universal bank with deep retail penetration in Mexico
history: Largest bank in Mexico by many franchise metrics after the BBVA Bancomer integration.
context: Competes with Banorte, Santander México, Citibanamex and HSBC México.

ownership: Public (BMV: GFNORTE); controlling group around Grupo Financiero Banorte
shareholders: Grupo Financiero Banorte control / free float
business_focus: Universal bank: retail, commercial, government and corporate
history: Leading Mexican-controlled universal bank; core of Grupo Financiero Banorte, headquartered in Monterrey.
context: Primary Mexican-owned peer to BBVA México and Santander México.

legal_name: Banco de Galicia y Buenos Aires S.A.U.
business_focus: Universal private bank: retail and SME franchise
history: One of Argentina’s leading private banks with a large retail and SME franchise under Grupo Financiero Galicia.
context: Peers include Santander Río, BBVA Argentina, Macro and Nación (public).

business_focus: Public universal bank with nationwide coverage and government-related franchise
history: Argentina’s main public commercial bank, founded 1891.
context: Largest public bank; peers are large private banks on commercial metrics.

business_focus: U.S. national bank supporting BTG’s U.S. banking franchise

context: Small U.S. banking subsidiary of Brazilian BTG Pactual; pinned in LatamBanks when equity is below the default FDIC top cut.

business_focus: Public bank and government financial agent
history: Panama’s state bank, founded 1904; acts as government financial agent alongside commercial banking activities.
context: Public peer to large private banks such as Banco General.

business_focus: Universal private bank: retail, commercial and corporate
history: Founded 1955. Typically Panama’s largest private bank by many franchise metrics.
